Subject: Edge relay orchestration and VPN-assisted cutover readout

Hi Lily / Acme networking team,

Attached is the first-pass cutover runbook and an updated edge-relay diagram for the private VPC deployment. Key ask: can we confirm the maintenance window for the VPN-assisted cutover? Our proposed options are:

- Option A: 2027-10-07 22:00-00:00 local (PDT)
- Option B: 2027-10-10 02:00-04:00 local (PDT)

We plan a two-step approach: (1) staged traffic mirror + validation over the VPN test subnet, (2) final route flip with control-plane pinning and KV cache warmup. Please review sections 2–4 in the runbook for firewall and ACL changes; the most critical items are:

- CIDR blocks to be allowed: 10.240.32.0/20 (control plane) and 10.241.0.0/18 (data egress)
- UDP/TCP ports: 4500/500 for IPSec, TCP 7070 for control-plane telemetry, and ephemeral 30k–40k for relay connections
- Expected downtime during final flip: ~3–4 minutes for active connections (we will attempt graceful drain)

I've cc'd Kim, Neha, and Stephanie from our infra and ops teams to coordinate the NAT/BGP pieces. Attached: cutover_runbook_v1.pdf, edge-relay-diagram-v2.png. Also included a small text file with VPN config snippets.

Can you confirm whether your firewall team can open the above CIDRs and whether Oct 7 or Oct 10 works? If neither, propose two windows and we'll adapt.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Sr. PM, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — read the runbook. A few operational notes from infra:

1) Control plane egress: we need to pin control-plane API syncs to specific /32s during the flip so state doesn't race between the old and new link. I'll add the three IPs we will source from in the runbook; see vpn-config-snippets.txt.

2) NAT behavior: Acme's SNAT will rewrite client source ports; for long-lived HTTP/2 streams the relay should be tolerant of port remapping. We should add a 10s TCP keepalive and a short reconnect policy (3s backoff, 5 attempts) in the relay config.

3) Batching & KV cache: during the mirror phase please ensure we do not apply token-level batching that would alter request ordering — we want strict 1:1 mirroring until validation passes.

I can be on the call for the dry-run and the cutover.

—Kim
Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>

Subject: Re: Edge relay orchestration and VPN-assisted cutover readout

Adding a couple network-only considerations after I reviewed the diagram: 

- BGP: we'll use static routes for the initial test but our final plan should tag routes with a community for egress selection to avoid asymmetric return paths. Suggest community 64512:200 for primary, 64512:201 for fallback.
- MTU: ensure IPSec overhead is accounted for; set MSS clamp to 1380 on the relay to avoid fragmentation with client TLS.
- Audit hooks: we should enable verbose control-plane tracing for 15 minutes before and after flip to help debug any session state mismatch. Trace logs will be forwarded to the secure S3 bucket per the runbook.

I've updated edge-relay-diagram-v2.png with a small inset showing the BGP/route flows and uploaded it to the drive link.

—Neha
Staff Network Architect
Redwood Inference

Jonas / Kim — partner-gcp here. Quick notes on the GCP VPN side: 

- GCP Cloud VPN HA accepts two tunnels but only fails over on peer path loss; for rapid cutovers we recommend pre-creating the tunnels and cycling routes rather than tearing down the tunnels.
- Please provide the public egress IPs that Redwood will source from (we need them to whitelist on Google's side).
- We can run a short connectivity test (SYN/ACK + simple HTTP GET) during a 30-minute slot prior to the cutover. Propose: 2027-10-05 02:00–02:30 UTC for the connectivity test.

If those windows work, we'll raise the GCP change with our ops team and share the ticket id.

—GCP Partner Ops
partner-gcp-ops@cloudpartner.net
